title: A Capabilities Approach to Studying Bias and Harm in Language Technologies

bias_targets.methodology: Proposes evaluating language technologies through the Capabilities Approach, shifting from English-centric resource allocation metrics to procedural community assessments that determine what diverse language communities can actually achieve based on their specific conversion factors.

Recommends a community-engaged procedural framework to identify harms and biases specific to the 'Majority World', evaluating technology based on community-defined capabilities and intersecting socioeconomic realities rather than WEIRD-centric (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic) standards.
